assessment.reason: The study develops and tests corrections for composite time trade-off as used in EQ-5D valuation. It directly uses EQ-5D-5L health states and an adapted EQ-VT protocol. The acknowledgement explicitly states that the EuroQol Research Foundation funded this study.

studies.label: Development and empirical evaluation of corrections for discounting and loss aversion in composite time trade-off
studies.family_rationale: The principal contribution is an extension and empirical test of a corrective method for cTTO. The method adjusts utilities for individual discounting and loss aversion, including utilities for states worse than dead. The study does not produce an EQ-5D value set.

items.statement: Loss aversion was common at both reference points, and the mean loss-aversion estimates did not differ significantly between the 10-year and 20-year reference points.

items.statement: Aggregate discounting was close to linear, but respondent-level discount functions were heterogeneous and included both positive and negative discounting.

items.statement: Corrected utilities were generally significantly lower than elicited and confirmed utilities. For state 35332, the constant-alternative correction was not significantly lower than the elicited utility.
source: Full article, Results, Elicited, confirmed and corrected cTTO utilities, paragraph after Figure 1

items.statement: The authors concluded that the downward effect of correction was largely driven by loss aversion rather than discounting.
source: Full article, Discussion, third paragraph

items.statement: Because corrected utilities were lower than confirmed utilities, the authors stated that the corrective approach might overcorrect, although the appropriate utility benchmark remains unclear.
source: Full article, Results, Elicited, confirmed and corrected cTTO utilities, paragraph after Figure 1
Full article, Discussion, fifth paragraph

items.statement: The authors interpreted the severe-state differences as evidence that the assumed reference point has an important effect on corrected lead-time TTO utilities.
source: Full article, Discussion, third paragraph

items.statement: The authors stated that heterogeneous discounting prevents the use of one mean discount function for all respondents and increases the task burden of valuation studies.
source: Full article, Discussion, second paragraph

items.statement: The authors concluded that the study provides a foundation for applying the corrective approach in practical health-state valuation, but whether and how loss aversion should be corrected remain open questions.
source: Full article, Discussion, final paragraph

items.statement: Correcting cTTO utilities adds measurement error from the loss-aversion and time-preference measures, especially because the non-parametric and direct methods use chained elicitation.
source: Full article, Discussion, limitations paragraph, first limitation

items.statement: Corrected utilities are not bounded at −1, while the validation scale was bounded at −1. This difference can partly explain why confirmed utilities were higher than corrected utilities and can create practical problems for worse-than-dead states.
source: Full article, Discussion, limitations paragraph, second limitation

items.statement: The approach models loss aversion only for life duration. This can give counterintuitive classifications of gained or lost years when the added or removed years are lived in a state worse than dead.
source: Full article, Discussion, limitations paragraph, third limitation
